claim: A CXO Advisory summary of Beckmeyer, Branger and Gayda reports retail traders lost about $70 million in aggregate on 0DTE S&P 500 index options, with average daily net loss rising from $184,000 to $358,000 after daily expirations began in May 2022 (CBOE data, Jan 2021 to Feb 2023). This is secondary coverage, not the paper's own text.
quote: Retail traders lost about $70 million in aggregate on 0DTE S&P 500 Index options, with average daily net loss rising from $184,000 to $358,000 after daily expirations began in May 2022
title: CXO Advisory: Retail 0DTE Option Trader Performance

claim: Beckmeyer, Branger and Gayda (version of 15 Dec 2023) state that retail investors lost $241,000 on an average day in S&P 500 0DTE options between Feb 2021 and Sep 2023, and $350,000 per day on average since daily expirations began in May 2022.
quote: between February 2021 and September 2023, retail investors lost $241,000 on an average day; since the introduction of a daily expiration calendar in May of 2022, this number has grown to average losses of $350,000 per day
title: Beckmeyer, Branger, Gayda: Retail Traders Love 0DTE Options... But Should They? (working paper, 15 Dec 2023)

claim: The same paper puts total retail losses at more than $125 million over the sample, of which more than $90 million came from transaction costs.
quote: retail investors together lost more than $125 million. More than $90 million of these losses are the result of the transaction costs, the remainder a result of poor positioning
title: Beckmeyer, Branger, Gayda: Retail Traders Love 0DTE Options... But Should They? (working paper, 15 Dec 2023)

claim: The same paper attributes the losses to single-leg trades, trades needing an upfront payment and trades in high-implied-volatility options; multi-leg trades were significantly more profitable.
quote: We find that single-leg trades, trades that require an upfront payment to be set up, and trades that use high-implied volatility options are responsible for these losses
title: Beckmeyer, Branger, Gayda: Retail Traders Love 0DTE Options... But Should They? (working paper, 15 Dec 2023)

claim: The same paper says roughly 60% of daily retail 0DTE losses come from transaction costs.
quote: Roughly 60% of daily losses are the result of transaction costs
title: Beckmeyer, Branger, Gayda: Retail Traders Love 0DTE Options... But Should They? (working paper, 15 Dec 2023)
